text.zh: 序幕
text.en: PROLOGUE

text.zh: 海的另一边
text.en: Across the Sea

text.zh: 大西洋
text.en: THE ATLANTIC

text.zh: 序幕
text.en: Prologue

text.zh: 一封信，把一个名字带离了海岛。
text.en: A letter carries a name beyond the island.

text.zh: 走近信件，读完序幕。
text.en: Approach the letter and read the prologue.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Opening

text.zh: 一封漂洋过海的信
text.en: A Letter Across the Atlantic

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Opening

text.zh: 他来自加勒比海。商行的账本教会他计算，海上的风暴教会他：一个人的处境，可能在一夜之间被改写。
text.en: He came from the Caribbean. A merchant's ledgers taught him to reckon; storms at sea taught him that a life could be rewritten overnight.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Opening

text.zh: 他把所见写成文字。有人读了那篇文章，开始相信，这个年轻人应该得到继续求学的机会。
text.en: He put what he had seen into words. People read them and began to believe this young man deserved the chance to continue his education.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Opening

text.zh: 我带不走那座岛。但我能带走纸上的每一个字。纽约有学校，有印刷机，也有人愿意争论未来。我要在那里找到我的位置。
text.en: I cannot take the island with me. But I can carry every word on the page. New York has schools, printing presses, and people willing to argue about the future. I will find my place there.

text.zh: 踏上纽约街头
text.en: Step into New York

text.zh: 第一幕 · 第一场
text.en: ACT I · SCENE 01

text.zh: 纽约，没有空位
text.en: New York Has No Empty Seats

text.zh: 纽约
text.en: NEW YORK

text.zh: 每条街都在争论。每个人都在选择。
text.en: Every street is arguing. Everyone is choosing.

text.zh: 依次读新闻、听争论，最后与伯尔交谈。
text.en: Read the news, hear the argument, then speak with Burr.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 今日号外
text.en: Today's Extra

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 港口的消息！英军动向、商船货价，还有一整版互相反驳的文章。
text.en: News from the harbor! British troop movements, cargo prices, and a whole page of writers contradicting each other.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 先给我一份。只有知道这座城在为什么争吵，我的文字才不会只是对着自己说话。
text.en: Give me a copy first. Until I know what this city is arguing about, my writing will only be a conversation with myself.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 街头的争论
text.en: An Argument in the Street

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 驻军越来越多。有人说军队保护生意，可我只想知道：他们保护的是谁作决定的权利？
text.en: More troops arrive every day. They say the army protects trade. But whose right to decide are they protecting?

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 没有王室和海军，这座港口靠什么维持秩序？你们把眼前的生计，押给一个还不存在的国家。
text.en: Without the Crown and its navy, what keeps order in this port? You would stake today's livelihood on a country that does not yet exist.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 这两个人都害怕失去手里的生活。但他们还没问过，谁有资格替另一方下注。
text.en: Both are afraid of losing the lives they have. Neither has asked who has the right to make that wager for the other.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 阿伦·伯尔
text.en: Aaron Burr

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 你听了很久。亚历山大·汉密尔顿，对吗？我读过你的文字。
text.en: You have been listening for a while. Alexander Hamilton, isn't it? I have read your work.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 那就省了介绍。你也听见了——他们谈论自由的时候，仿佛每个人说的是不同的东西。
text.en: Then we can skip the introductions. You heard them too: when they speak of freedom, they seem to mean entirely different things.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 先弄清楚谁在听，再决定说多少。局势会变；公开说过的话，会留下来。
text.en: Learn who is listening before you decide how much to say. Circumstances change. Words spoken in public remain.

context: field: prompt / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 伯尔建议你暂缓表态。你如何回应？
text.en: Burr advises you to wait before taking a side. How do you respond?

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 先观察，弄清各方的立场。
text.en: Observe first and understand where each side stands.

context: field: hint / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 克制 · 理解局势
text.en: Restraint · Read the situation

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 很好。耐心也能是一种行动。我们去酒馆，那里比街头容易听见真话。
text.en: Good. Patience can be a form of action. Come to the tavern. It is easier to hear people speak plainly there.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 那你呢？你自己相信什么？
text.en: And you? What do you believe?

context: field: hint / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 追问 · 了解伯尔
text.en: Ask further · Understand Burr

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 我相信，作决定之前应该把人看清楚。你这个问题，让我更想认识你了。走吧。
text.en: I believe in knowing people before making decisions. That question makes me more interested in knowing you. Come along.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 我支持革命。现在就可以写下我的名字。
text.en: I support the revolution. You can put my name to it now.

context: field: hint / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 公开表态 · 承担风险
text.en: Take a public stand · Accept the risk

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Arrival

text.zh: 我听见了。整条街也听见了。希望你准备好了，为这么响亮的名字负责。
text.en: I heard you. So did the whole street. I hope you are ready to answer for a name spoken that loudly.

text.zh: 进入酒馆
text.en: Enter the Tavern

text.zh: 叙事时间压缩 · 汉密尔顿于 1772 年抵达纽约；本章将早年的抵达与 1776 年的革命局势合并呈现。
text.en: Compressed chronology · Hamilton arrived in New York in 1772. This chapter combines his arrival with the revolutionary tensions of 1776.

text.zh: 第一幕 · 第二场
text.en: ACT I · SCENE 02

text.zh: 同一张桌子
text.en: At the Same Table

text.zh: 纽约 · 酒馆
text.en: NEW YORK · TAVERN

text.zh: 他们并不相信同一种未来。今晚，他们坐在一起。
text.en: They do not imagine the same future. Tonight, they share a table.

text.zh: 自由选择顺序，与劳伦斯、拉法耶特和穆利根各谈一次。
text.en: Speak once with Laurens, Lafayette, and Mulligan in any order.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 劳伦斯的问题
text.en: Laurens's Question

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 我们把自由写得那么大，却总把某些人留在句子外面。一个仍允许奴役的国家，准备怎样解释自己的自由？
text.en: We write freedom in such large letters, yet always leave certain people outside the sentence. How will a country that still permits slavery explain its freedom?

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 你要的答案，恐怕会让这张桌子安静下来。
text.en: The answer you want may bring this table to a silence.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 那就让它安静。你认为现在最重要的是什么？
text.en: Then let it fall silent. What do you think matters most right now?

context: field: prompt / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 革命应该先回答哪一个问题？
text.en: Which question should the revolution answer first?

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 先维持秩序，让人们活过这场战争。
text.en: Preserve order so people survive the war.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 活下来当然重要。可有些人一直在等“以后”，我们不能再轻易替他们说这个词。
text.en: Surviving matters, of course. But some people have always been told to wait until later. We cannot keep saying that on their behalf.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 谁来作决定，谁又有权提出反对？
text.en: Who gets to decide, and who has the right to object?

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 那么，记得把被排除的人也算进去。换一个掌权的人，还不够。
text.en: Then remember to include those who have been excluded. Replacing the people in power is not enough.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 自由的承诺，应当包含被奴役的人。
text.en: The promise of freedom must include enslaved people.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 我愿意和这样的人并肩。但当这个承诺开始让盟友不舒服时，你还得说下去。
text.en: I would stand beside someone who believes that. But when that promise begins to trouble our allies, you must keep saying it.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 拉法耶特的问题
text.en: Lafayette's Question

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 我横渡大西洋，不是为了旁观。可勇气不能替士兵装满口粮。面对更强的军队，你准备把力气用在哪里？
text.en: I did not cross the Atlantic to watch. But courage cannot fill a soldier's ration bag. Against a stronger army, where will you put your effort?

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 每一条路都要付代价。区别在于，我们愿不愿意自己选择。
text.en: Every path has a price. The difference is whether we are willing to choose for ourselves.

context: field: prompt / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 怎样让革命继续向前？
text.en: How do we carry the revolution forward?

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 保持谈判，为居民争取喘息。
text.en: Keep negotiating to give civilians room to breathe.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 可以。但谈判桌也需要有人在外面守着。别把喘息误当成终点。
text.en: Perhaps. But someone must stand guard outside the negotiating room. Do not mistake a breath of air for the end of the journey.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 建立联盟，把孤军变成共同事业。
text.en: Build alliances and turn an isolated struggle into a shared cause.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 那你得学会听见盟友的需要。共同事业，不能只有一个人的声音。
text.en: Then you must learn to hear what your allies need. A shared cause cannot speak in only one person's voice.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 公开争取独立，不再等待许可。
text.en: Demand independence openly, without waiting for permission.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 够直接。我喜欢。但说完这句话，下一步就该准备行军了。
text.en: Direct enough. I like it. But after those words, the next step is preparing to march.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 穆利根的问题
text.en: Mulligan's Question

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 大道理我听够了。明早有十个人愿意帮忙，一家印刷铺肯赊账，还有一辆空车。汉密尔顿，你怎么用？
text.en: I've heard enough grand ideas. Tomorrow, ten people will help, a printer will extend credit, and there's an empty wagon. Hamilton, how will you use them?

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 你给我的不是十个人，是十个人各自认识的那条街。
text.en: You have given me more than ten people. You have given me every street they know.

context: field: prompt / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 把今晚的话，变成明早的哪件事？
text.en: What will tonight's words become tomorrow morning?

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 印一份清楚的传单，让每条街接着讨论。
text.en: Print a clear pamphlet to keep the conversation going in every street.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 行。少写几个漂亮词，多写几句他们能讲给邻居听的话。
text.en: Good. Fewer elegant phrases, more lines they can repeat to their neighbors.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 先送补给，让愿意加入的人吃上饭。
text.en: Deliver supplies first so people willing to join us can eat.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 车我来找。愿意做这种不显眼的事，才有人下次还来找你。
text.en: I'll find the wagon. Be willing to do the work no one notices, and people will come to you again.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 召集公开集会，今天就让更多人听见。
text.en: Call a public meeting and make more people hear us today.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Tavern

text.zh: 场地可以有。巡逻队一来，你可不能只顾着自己的演说。
text.en: We can find a place. But when the patrol arrives, you cannot think only of your speech.

text.zh: 走向公开辩论
text.en: Go to the Public Debate

text.zh: 读完问题后有 {0} 秒回应。三人可按任意顺序交谈；超时保持沉默，Esc 可暂停。
text.en: You have {0} seconds to answer after the question. Speak to the three companions in any order; timeout means silence, and Esc pauses the game.

text.zh: 第一幕 · 第三场
text.en: ACT I · SCENE 03

text.zh: 把声音放到街上
text.en: Take Your Voice to the Street

text.zh: 纽约 · 公共广场
text.en: NEW YORK · PUBLIC SQUARE

text.zh: 革命初期
text.en: Early Revolution

text.zh: 纸上的争论，终于有了听众。
text.en: The arguments on the page have found an audience.

text.zh: 争取群众支持，击破论点，观察伯尔的反应。
text.en: Win public support, challenge the argument, and see how Burr responds.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Debate

text.zh: 公开回应
text.en: Answer in Public

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Debate

text.zh: 脱离英国之后，商船由谁护送，货物卖给谁？你们用自由作保证，却要每一个家庭拿生计来冒险。
text.en: Once you break from Britain, who escorts the ships, and who buys the cargo? You offer freedom as a guarantee, but ask every family to risk its livelihood.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Debate

text.zh: 这也是我想问的。没有明天的面包，今天的口号有什么用？
text.en: That is what I want to know. Without tomorrow's bread, what good are today's slogans?

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Debate

text.zh: 他们在等你的回答。把问题听完。
text.en: They are waiting for your answer. Hear the whole question.

text.zh: 带着名声走进军营
text.en: Bring Your Reputation into Camp

text.zh: 第二幕 · 第一场
text.en: ACT II · SCENE 01

text.zh: 笔，比军刀更近
text.en: The Pen Comes Before the Sword

text.zh: 大陆军 · 总部
text.en: CONTINENTAL ARMY · HEADQUARTERS

text.zh: 他想要战场。将军先递来一叠信件。
text.en: He wants the battlefield. The general hands him a stack of letters.

text.zh: 回应华盛顿，并决定怎样整理军令。
text.en: Answer Washington, then organize his dispatches.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 总司令的提议
text.en: The Commander's Offer

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 我看过你的文章。你能把事情写清楚。但军中需要的，还有把事情做完。
text.en: I have read your essays. You make matters clear. But an army also needs people who finish the work.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 我希望带兵。我的能力不该只留在信纸上。
text.en: I want to lead troops. My ability should not stay on the page.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 军令、情报、补给。写错一个地点，也会有人付出代价。我需要副官。你愿意从这里开始吗？
text.en: Orders, intelligence, supplies. A wrong place name can cost lives. I need an aide. Are you willing to begin here?

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 你的文章已经传进军营。我也听说了街上的争论。让别人注意你，你很擅长；让别人依靠你，是另一回事。
text.en: Your essays have reached camp. So has news of the argument in the street. You are good at drawing attention. Making yourself dependable is another matter.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 那么给我一支队伍。我愿意用行动证明。
text.en: Then give me a company. I am willing to prove myself through action.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 先做我的副官。军令、情报和补给，也决定着一支队伍能不能回来。你愿意承担吗？
text.en: Serve as my aide first. Orders, intelligence, and supplies also decide whether a company comes home. Will you take that responsibility?

context: field: prompt / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 你如何回应这份尚不是理想的职位？
text.en: How do you respond to a position that is not yet the one you want?

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 接受副官职位，先完成眼前的责任。
text.en: Accept the post and fulfill the responsibility at hand.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 很好。今晚有几封信，不能等到明天。
text.en: Good. Several letters tonight cannot wait until tomorrow.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 接受，同时明确争取未来的指挥机会。
text.en: Accept, while making clear that you want a future command.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 我听清了你的要求。你也要听清我的：用现在的职责，证明我能交给你下一份职责。
text.en: I have heard your request. Hear mine as well: prove through your present duties that I can trust you with the next ones.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 我属于战场，应当立刻得到指挥权。
text.en: I belong on the battlefield and should be given command now.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 这里没有人只凭“应当”获得命令权。今晚你仍然从这些军令开始。
text.en: No one here receives command merely because he thinks he should. Tonight, you will still begin with these dispatches.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 写下军令
text.en: Write the Dispatch

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 北线的部队需要补给。驻地、出发时间、目的地都在这些报告里。给军需官一份能够执行的命令。
text.en: The northern troops need supplies. Their camp, the departure time, and the destination are in these reports. Give the quartermaster an order he can carry out.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Washington

text.zh: 一页纸。不能让收信人猜测，也不能让他在一段漂亮文字里寻找自己的任务。
text.en: One page. The reader must not have to guess, or search through fine prose to find his task.

text.zh: 翻过战争中的几年
text.en: Turn the Pages of the War

text.zh: 第二幕 · 第二场
text.en: ACT II · SCENE 02

text.zh: 终于，轮到你下令
text.en: At Last, the Order Is Yours

text.zh: 约克镇
text.en: YORKTOWN

text.zh: 多年信件之后，等待已久的命令终于抵达。
text.en: After years of letters, the long-awaited order arrives.

text.zh: 接过指挥权，作出选择，见证约克镇的结局。
text.en: Take command, make your choices, and witness Yorktown's outcome.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 接过指挥权
text.en: Take Command

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 1781 年，法美联军围困约克镇。数年的行军、军令与争执，终于把汉密尔顿带到一座英军堡垒前。
text.en: In 1781, French and American forces surrounded Yorktown. Years of marches, dispatches, and disputes brought Hamilton to the foot of a British redoubt.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 你得到这次指挥机会。我要看到的，是一个能对整支队伍负责的军官。严格执行计划，别把它变成你一个人的证明。
text.en: You have this command. What I expect is an officer responsible for his whole company. Follow the plan. Do not turn it into a private test of your worth.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 我明白。等了这么久，我不能只想着自己如何被看见。
text.en: I understand. After waiting so long, I cannot think only of how I will be seen.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 1781 年，法美联军围困约克镇。数年的行军与军令，把汉密尔顿带到一座英军堡垒前。
text.en: In 1781, French and American forces surrounded Yorktown. Years of marches and dispatches brought Hamilton to the foot of a British redoubt.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 你证明了自己能承担责任。这支队伍交给你。按计划行动；现场需要判断时，我相信你知道命令背后的目的。
text.en: You have proved you can carry responsibility. These troops are yours. Follow the plan; when judgment is needed, I trust you to understand the purpose behind the order.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 这一次，纸上的名字会和我一起向前。我会记住，他们要跟随的不是一句漂亮的话。
text.en: This time, the names on the page will move forward beside me. I will remember that they need more than a fine sentence to follow.

context: field: prompt / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 出发前，你给部下的第一道指令是？
text.en: Before setting out, what is your first instruction to the troops?

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 核对各队的职责，等共同信号再推进。
text.en: Confirm each squad's role and wait for the common signal.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 每一队都要知道身旁的人在哪里。听到信号，一起前进。
text.en: Every squad must know where the others are. When the signal comes, we move together.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 我走在最前面，你们跟紧。
text.en: I will lead from the front. Stay close.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 我会先走出去。但看清信号，别因为跟随我而忘了自己的位置。
text.en: I will step out first. But watch the signal. Do not lose your own position by following mine.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 说明共同目标，让每个人知道为何出发。
text.en: Explain the shared objective so everyone knows why we are going.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 我们要打开围城的一道缺口。记住身边的人，记住回来的路。现在，各就各位。
text.en: We are opening a breach in the siege. Remember the person beside you, and remember the way back. Now, take your positions.

context: field: label / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 炮声之后
text.en: After the Guns

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 汉密尔顿率队攻下十号堡垒，法军攻下相邻的九号堡垒。围城继续收紧。
text.en: Hamilton's troops took Redoubt No. 10, while French forces took the neighboring Redoubt No. 9. The siege tightened.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 数日后，英军在约克镇投降。胜利来自许多人的共同作战。战争尚未正式结束，但局势已经改变。
text.en: Days later, British forces surrendered at Yorktown. Victory belonged to many people fighting together. The war had not formally ended, but its course had changed.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: interactions / field: Yorktown

text.zh: 那些从前只能写进信里的愿望，现在终于有了重量。明天，还会有人问，我们准备拿这个胜利做什么。
text.en: The hopes I once could only put in letters finally have weight. Tomorrow, someone will ask what we intend to do with this victory.

text.zh: 阅读你的革命侧写
text.en: Read Your Revolutionary Portrait

text.zh: 亚历山大·汉密尔顿
text.en: Alexander Hamilton

text.zh: 写作者 · 寻找位置的人
text.en: Writer · Searching for a place

text.zh: 阿伦·伯尔
text.en: Aaron Burr

text.zh: 律师 · 谨慎的观察者
text.en: Lawyer · A cautious observer

text.zh: 乔治·华盛顿
text.en: George Washington

text.zh: 大陆军总司令
text.en: Commander of the Continental Army

text.zh: 约翰·劳伦斯
text.en: John Laurens

text.zh: 理想主义者
text.en: Idealist

text.zh: 拉法耶特
text.en: Marquis de Lafayette

text.zh: 来自法国的志愿者
text.en: A volunteer from France

text.zh: 赫拉克勒斯·穆利根
text.en: Hercules Mulligan

text.zh: 裁缝 · 街头的组织者
text.en: Tailor · Organizer in the streets

text.zh: 保皇派撰稿人
text.en: Loyalist Pamphleteer

text.zh: 公开辩论者
text.en: Public speaker

text.zh: 报童
text.en: Newsboy

text.zh: 港口的消息
text.en: News from the harbor

text.zh: 纽约市民
text.en: New York Citizen

text.zh: 街头的声音
text.en: A voice from the street

text.zh: 伊莱莎 · 记录者
text.en: Eliza · The Chronicler

text.zh: 在纸页之间，留下他们的故事
text.en: Keeping their story on the page

text.zh: 事实
text.en: Facts

text.zh: 原则
text.en: Principle

text.zh: 反击
text.en: Attack

text.zh: 动员
text.en: Rally

text.zh: 稳定削弱可信度
text.en: Steadily weaken credibility

text.zh: 争取支持与锐气
text.en: Build support and momentum

text.zh: 高收益；失拍反噬
text.en: High reward; a missed beat backfires

text.zh: 迅速聚拢人群；论证变弱
text.en: Rally the crowd quickly; weaken the argument

text.zh: 贸易与生计
text.en: Trade and Livelihood

text.zh: 脱离英国之后，商船由谁护送，货物卖给谁？你们让每个家庭用明天的面包支付自由。
text.en: After leaving Britain, who will escort the ships and buy the cargo? You ask each family to pay for freedom with tomorrow's bread.

text.zh: 听众想知道具体的成本。事实更有分量。
text.en: The audience wants concrete costs. Facts carry more weight here.

text.zh: 把税负与贸易限制也算进去。
text.en: Count taxes and trade restrictions too.

text.zh: 承担代价的人应有决定权。
text.en: Those who pay should have a say.

text.zh: 你为何只计算改变的代价？
text.en: Why count only the costs of change?

text.zh: 让码头的人说说他们的账本。
text.en: Let the dockworkers open their ledgers.

text.zh: 谁来决定
text.en: Who Decides?

text.zh: 帝国的议会已经替各地考虑过了。若每座港口都要求自己决定，法律还剩下什么？
text.en: Parliament has already considered every region. If each port insists on deciding for itself, what is left of the law?

text.zh: 争论落在代表权上。原则更有分量。
text.en: The question is representation. Principle carries more weight here.

text.zh: 把殖民地的代表席位列出来。
text.en: List the colonies' seats in Parliament.

text.zh: 服从法律，也应参与制定。
text.en: Those who obey laws should help make them.

text.zh: 考虑过，不等于听过我们的声音。
text.en: Considering us is not the same as hearing us.

text.zh: 谁愿意让别人决定自己的税？
text.en: Who wants others to decide their taxes?

text.zh: 承诺与责任
text.en: Promises and Responsibility

text.zh: 倡议革命的人只会写文章。等粮食短缺，他们会让穷人承担后果。
text.en: The advocates of revolution only write essays. When food runs short, they will leave the poor to bear the consequences.

text.zh: 人群希望亲自说出处境。动员更有效。
text.en: People want to speak for themselves. Rallying them works better here.

text.zh: 补给方案与责任人必须公开。
text.en: Publish the supply plan and those responsible.

text.zh: 自由不能只属于有余粮的人。
text.en: Freedom cannot belong only to the well-fed.

text.zh: 你也没给穷人留下别的出路。
text.en: You have offered the poor no other path.

text.zh: 请工人和店主自己提出条件。
text.en: Let workers and shopkeepers name their terms.

text.zh: 秩序的代价
text.en: The Price of Order

text.zh: 驻军只为保护秩序。既然你们没有做错什么，为何害怕更多巡逻？
text.en: The garrison is only here to keep order. If you have done nothing wrong, why fear more patrols?

text.zh: 对方把质疑等同于心虚。反击能揭开漏洞。
text.en: Your opponent equates questioning with guilt. An attack can expose the flaw.

text.zh: 检查驻军的权限与费用。
text.en: Examine the garrison's powers and costs.

text.zh: 权力仍需得到被治理者同意。
text.en: Power still needs the consent of the governed.

text.zh: 要求解释，何时成了认错？
text.en: Since when is asking for an explanation a confession?

text.zh: 请居民讲讲巡逻带来的变化。
text.en: Let residents describe what patrols have changed.

text.zh: 战争的风险
text.en: The Risk of War

text.zh: 帝国拥有舰队和资金。你们连统一的军需账册都没有，却要把大家带进战争。
text.en: The empire has fleets and money. You do not even have a common supply ledger, yet you would lead everyone into war.

text.zh: 此刻需要可执行的办法。事实更有分量。
text.en: This calls for a workable plan. Facts carry more weight here.

text.zh: 统一账册，逐项落实补给。
text.en: Unify the ledgers and secure supplies item by item.

text.zh: 危险不能取消选择的权利。
text.en: Danger does not erase the right to choose.

text.zh: 你的胜算只是让我们永远服从。
text.en: Your only plan is that we obey forever.

text.zh: 把愿意承担的工作写在这里。
text.en: Write down the work you are willing to do.

text.zh: 未来属于谁
text.en: Whose Future?

text.zh: 即使赢了，谁能保证新掌权的人更好？你们只是把一种不确定换成另一种。
text.en: Even if you win, who guarantees the new rulers will be better? You are exchanging one uncertainty for another.

text.zh: 争论来到制度与约束。原则更有分量。
text.en: The question is institutions and limits on power. Principle carries more weight here.

text.zh: 将任期与问责写进制度。
text.en: Put terms of office and accountability into law.

text.zh: 让人民保留更换掌权者的权利。
text.en: Keep the people's right to replace their rulers.

text.zh: 没有保证，不等于现状无需改变。
text.en: No guarantee does not mean no need for change.

text.zh: 把你们不愿再接受的事说出来。
text.en: Tell us what you will no longer accept.

text.zh: 你沉默了一会儿。没关系，先听听其他人的想法；这张桌子还会留一个位置。
text.en: You fall silent for a moment. That's all right. Listen to the others first; there will still be a place for you at this table.

text.zh: 先别把报纸折起来，墨还没干呢。
text.en: Don't fold the paper yet. The ink is still wet.

text.zh: 等等，你还少了这几张。我替你压住它们。
text.en: Wait, these pages are yours too. Let me hold them down.

text.zh: 多谢！你就是刚才买报的先生。我会记得你的名字。
text.en: Thank you! You are the gentleman who just bought a paper. I will remember your name.

text.zh: 报纸都收好了，汉密尔顿先生！这一回，风抢不过我。
text.en: All the papers are safe, Mr. Hamilton! The wind will not get them this time.

text.zh: 信纸背面的名字
text.en: A Name on the Back

text.zh: 翻过信纸，背面留着几次试写的姓名。墨迹有深有浅，最后一次落笔格外清楚。
text.en: On the back of the letter, a name has been written several times. The ink varies in darkness; the final attempt is especially clear.

text.zh: 亚历山大·汉密尔顿。先把名字写稳，再让人记住它。
text.en: Alexander Hamilton. First, write the name with a steady hand. Then give people a reason to remember it.

text.zh: 这个名字已经写下。下一页，要写什么？
text.en: The name is on the page. What will go on the next one?

text.zh: 交还报纸
text.en: Return the Newspaper

text.zh: 我在酒馆后面找到了这些报纸。拿好，别再让风抢走了。
text.en: I found these pages behind the tavern. Hold them tight so the wind cannot snatch them again.

text.zh: 汉密尔顿。希望下次让你忙起来的，是值得传开的消息。
text.en: Hamilton. I hope next time it is news worth sharing that keeps you busy.

text.zh: 伯尔的页边批注
text.en: Burr's Margin Notes

text.zh: 你在这句旁边写了问号：谁来承担代价？
text.en: You put a question mark beside this sentence: who bears the cost?

text.zh: 一句话让自己满意很容易。试试让付出代价的人也愿意听下去。
text.en: It is easy to satisfy yourself with a sentence. Try keeping the attention of the people who must pay its price.

text.zh: 你怎样回应伯尔的批注？
text.en: How do you respond to Burr's note?

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice

text.zh: 请指出我还没有回答的部分。
text.en: Show me what I have not answered yet.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice

text.zh: 从他们最具体的担忧开始。你愿意改进论据，我愿意继续听。
text.en: Begin with their most concrete worry. If you are willing to improve your argument, I am willing to keep listening.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice

text.zh: 下一次，把这个问题当面抛给我。
text.en: Next time, put that question to me in public.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice

text.zh: 好。我会认真准备。你最好也给答案留一点准备的时间。
text.en: Very well. I will prepare seriously. You would do well to give your answer some preparation too.

text.zh: 问号还在这里。写出答案之前，不必急着擦掉它。
text.en: The question mark is still here. There is no hurry to erase it before you have an answer.

text.zh: 未完成的演说草稿
text.en: An Unfinished Speech

text.zh: 空桌上留着一张草稿，末行只有半句：如果我们的声音值得被听见……
text.en: A draft lies on an empty table. Its final line stops halfway: if our voices deserve to be heard...

text.zh: 这里还缺一句愿意公开承担的话。
text.en: It needs a sentence someone is willing to stand behind in public.

text.zh: 补完草稿的最后一句。
text.en: Finish the last sentence.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice

text.zh: 就把主张说清，也让人追问。
text.en: Then state our case clearly, and let people question it.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice

text.zh: 写在纸上还不够。我会把这句话带到街上。
text.en: The page is only a beginning. I will take this sentence into the street.

text.zh: 最后一行写完了。到了广场，就没有纸张替我挡住目光。
text.en: The last line is finished. In the square, no sheet of paper will stand between me and their eyes.

text.zh: 面包与货价
text.en: Bread and Prices

text.zh: 这张账单上的面包和运费，都被重新改过。你最担心哪一项？
text.en: The bread and freight prices on this bill have both been revised. Which worries you most?

text.zh: 我担心付完今天的钱，明天又不够。你们谈未来时，也把这一餐算进去。
text.en: I worry that after paying today, I will not have enough tomorrow. When you speak about the future, count this meal too.

text.zh: 我记住了。你不该先放下自己的生活，才有资格谈自由。
text.en: I will remember. You should not have to set your life aside before you can speak about freedom.

text.zh: 账单还在，问题也是。谢谢你先问了我们的日子。
text.en: The bill is still here, and so is the question. Thank you for asking about our lives first.

text.zh: 争论散了，明天还是要开门做生意。我会看你们怎样兑现说过的话。
text.en: The argument is over, but tomorrow we still have to open for business. I will watch how you follow through on what you said.

text.zh: 错置的军需便条
text.en: A Misfiled Supply Note

text.zh: 外封写着北侧驻地，正文却让车队往东。我得先核对，再送出去。
text.en: The cover says the northern camp, but the text sends the wagons east. I should check before this goes out.

text.zh: 正文才是这批补给的目的地。发现一处不一致，就先把它弄清楚。
text.en: The text gives the destination for this shipment. When you find a discrepancy, resolve it first.

text.zh: 按核对结果修正便条。
text.en: Correct the note after checking it.

context: field: text / field: options / field: choice

text.zh: 修正外封，标明核对后的目的地。
text.en: Correct the cover and mark the verified destination.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice

text.zh: 现在内外一致了。收信人不必替我们猜测。
text.en: The cover and the text now agree. The recipient will not have to guess for us.

context: field: text / field: reply / field: options / field: choice

text.zh: 很好。可靠，常常从这种小处开始。
text.en: Good. Reliability often begins with details like this.

text.zh: 便条已经核对。下一封也要经得起同样的检查。
text.en: The note has been checked. The next one deserves the same care.

text.zh: 这一批便条已经归档。记住：地点和时间，都要让收信人看得明白。
text.en: These notes have been filed. Remember: the recipient must be able to read both the place and the time clearly.

text.zh: 文件末尾的签名
text.en: A Signature on the Dispatch

text.zh: 当初在信纸背面写这个名字，只盼着有人记住。
text.en: When I wrote this name on the back of that letter, I only hoped someone would remember it.

text.zh: 现在，名字落在军令下面。有人会照着它出发，也有人在等他们回来。
text.en: Now it goes beneath an order. People will set out because of it, and others will wait for them to return.

text.zh: 同一个名字，已经承担了不同的重量。
text.en: The same name now carries a different weight.

text.zh: 这张文件还留着签名的位置。落笔以前，先确认每一处细节。
text.en: This document still has a space for a signature. Before signing, check every detail.

text.zh: 请伯尔评价论据
text.en: Ask Burr About Your Argument

text.zh: 你认为我的论据站得住吗？我想听具体的。
text.en: Do you think my argument holds up? I want specifics.

text.zh: 你愿意让人追问，这一点站得住。接下来，把每项主张和承担它的人连起来。
text.en: Your willingness to be questioned holds up. Next, connect each claim to the people who must bear it.

text.zh: 我会继续补全。也请你继续指出空缺。
text.en: I will keep filling in the gaps. Keep pointing them out.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants

text.zh: 你在页边留下的问号，我一直记得。今天，我回答得更完整了吗？
text.en: I remembered the question mark in your margin. Was my answer more complete today?

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants

text.zh: 你开始把听众的顾虑放进论证了。接下来，让每项主张都找到愿意承担它的人。
text.en: You have begun to bring the audience's concerns into your argument. Next, find the people willing to carry each proposal through.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants

text.zh: 那么，把新的问号也留下吧。
text.en: Then leave me the next question mark.

text.zh: 肯继续修正论据的人，值得继续听。
text.en: Someone willing to keep revising an argument is worth hearing again.

text.zh: 向伯尔约下一场辩论
text.en: Challenge Burr to Another Debate

text.zh: 下一次，由你来回应我？你总不能一直站在场边。
text.en: Next time, will you answer me? You cannot stay at the edge of the square forever.

text.zh: 可以。但我会挑你最不愿停下来回答的问题。
text.en: I will. But I will choose the question you are least willing to stop and answer.

text.zh: 那就带着问题来。我会带着答案。
text.en: Then bring your question. I will bring an answer.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants

text.zh: 页边的挑战还算数。下一次，由你来回应我？
text.en: The challenge in the margin still stands. Next time, will you answer me?

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants

text.zh: 我记得。也已经开始准备。别把我没有抢着开口，当成我无话可说。
text.en: I remember, and I have begun preparing. Do not mistake my waiting to speak for having nothing to say.

context: field: text / field: lines / field: variants

text.zh: 好。那我也不能停在今天的答案上。
text.en: Good. Then I cannot settle for the answers I gave today.

text.zh: 约定还在。我们都还有准备的时间。
text.en: The challenge stands. We both still have time to prepare.

text.zh: 你就是帮报童收过纸的人吧？我记得你的名字。说吧，我们听着。
text.en: You helped the newsboy gather his papers, did you not? I remember your name. Go on. We are listening.

text.zh: 汉密尔顿？有人向我提起过你。我愿意先听听你的回答。
text.en: Hamilton? Someone mentioned you to me. I am willing to hear your answer.

text.zh: 酒馆里那句写完的话，该拿出来接受追问了。
text.en: It is time to bring that sentence from the tavern into the open and let people question it.

text.zh: 我会走到人群面前，把主张说清楚。
text.en: I will step before the crowd and make my case clear.

text.zh: 先把他们的问题听完整。稳稳地回答，也是一种承担。
text.en: First, hear the whole question. A measured answer can carry responsibility too.

text.zh: 刚才账单上的那一餐，请记得放进你的答案里。
text.en: Remember to include the meal on that bill in your answer.

text.zh: 你核对过那张便条。现在，让每一份军令都经得起同样的检查。
text.en: You checked that supply note. Now give every dispatch the same care.

text.zh: 你愿意承担眼前的职责，我就从这几封军令开始相信你。
text.en: You have accepted the duty before you. These dispatches are where I begin to place my trust in you.

text.zh: 你从核对一张便条开始证明可靠。今晚，同样的细心也要跟着队伍出发。
text.en: You began proving dependable by checking a supply note. Tonight, take that same care into the field.

text.zh: 我争取这一刻很久了。现在，我会让这份勇气带着责任一起向前。
text.en: I have worked for this moment for a long time. Now I will carry responsibility forward with my courage.

text.zh: 不必抢过每个人的脚步。我要把他们一起带到目标前。
text.en: I do not need to outrun everyone. I need to bring them to the objective together.

text.zh: 你认出了军令签名与旧信背面的同一个名字。它从被记住的愿望，变成了对他人的责任。
text.en: You recognized the same name beneath a dispatch and on the back of the old letter. A wish to be remembered had become a responsibility to others.

text.zh: 出发前，你看见了信纸背面反复写下的名字。旅程从那个想被记住的愿望开始。
text.en: Before setting out, you found the name written repeatedly on the back of the letter. The journey began with that wish to be remembered.

text.zh: 在军营，你核对并修正了错置的军需便条。信任也从一个写准的目的地开始。
text.en: In camp, you checked and corrected a misfiled supply note. Trust also began with a destination written correctly.

text.zh: 辩论前，你听市民谈起面包与货价，把一个家庭的生活带进了广场的问题。
text.en: Before the debate, you listened to a citizen speak about bread and prices, bringing a family's livelihood into the question in the square.

text.zh: 你帮报童收回了被风吹散的纸张。有人先记住你的善意，才记住你的主张。
text.en: You helped the newsboy gather pages scattered by the wind. Someone remembered your kindness before your arguments.

text.zh: 你补完了酒馆里的演说草稿，随后把纸上的一句话带到了人群面前。
text.en: You finished a speech draft in the tavern, then brought a sentence from the page before the crowd.

text.zh: 在纽约，你请伯尔指出论证的空缺。他在页边留下的问号，也成了继续交谈的理由。
text.en: In New York, you asked Burr to point out gaps in your argument. His question mark in the margin became a reason to keep talking.

text.en: In New York, you turned Burr's margin note into an invitation to debate. He began preparing seriously to answer you.

text.zh: 初到纽约，你选择先观察。克制，也是你亲手作出的决定。
text.en: On arriving in New York, you chose to observe. Restraint, too, was a decision you made for yourself.

text.zh: 面对公开质疑，你选择厘清事实，让争论落到可以回答的问题上。
text.en: Under public challenge, you clarified the facts and brought the argument to questions that could be answered.

text.zh: 面对公开质疑，你把决定权放在中心，追问谁有资格选择未来。
text.en: Under public challenge, you put the right to decide at the center and asked who could choose the future.

text.zh: 面对公开质疑，你强硬揭开对方论证的偏向，也让冲突更加鲜明。
text.en: Under public challenge, you forcefully exposed the bias in your opponent's argument, sharpening the conflict.

text.zh: 面对公开质疑，你让现场的人加入，让个人的声音成为众人的讨论。
text.en: Under public challenge, you brought the audience into the discussion and turned one voice into many.

text.en: You won a command, but Washington's trust remained limited. Opportunity and recognition had not yet become the same thing.

text.zh: 第一次下令时，你先说明目标，希望每个人都知道自己为何出发。

text.zh: 伯尔对你的尊重与竞争心同时增长。他认真看待你的能力，也更在意你会走向哪里。
text.en: Burr's respect and rivalry both grew. He takes your ability seriously and watches more closely where it may lead you.

text.en: Conversation with Burr

text.zh: 街口相遇
text.en: AT THE CROSSROADS

text.zh: 阿伦·伯尔
text.en: Aaron Burr

text.zh: 刚下船？纽约的路比地图上窄，机会倒比地图上多。你在找谁？
text.en: Fresh off the boat? New York has narrower streets than its maps suggest—and more opportunities. Who are you looking for?

text.zh: 每个来到这里的年轻人，都觉得自己有话要说。你呢？
text.en: Every young man who arrives here thinks he has something to say. And you?

text.zh: 那就先看看人们为什么停下来听。酒馆就在那边。走近一点，你会听到这座城真正关心的事。
text.en: Then notice what makes people stop and listen. The tavern is over there. Walk closer, and you will hear what this city really cares about.

text.zh: 水岸是个好起点。船带来消息，人把消息变成立场。先走一圈，再决定你想站在哪一边。
text.en: The waterfront is a good place to begin. Ships bring news; people turn news into convictions. Walk around before you choose a side.

text.zh: 不必急着回答。街道一直在这里。去看看酒馆和水岸，再回来也不迟。
text.en: There is no need to answer yet. The streets will still be here. Visit the tavern and the waterfront; you can always return.

text.zh: 我想让这座城听见我。
text.en: I want this city to hear me.

text.zh: 先带我认识这座城。
text.en: First, let me get to know it.

text.en: A corner of New York

text.zh: 第一幕 · 初到纽约
text.en: ACT I · ARRIVAL

text.zh: 1776 · 一个名字尚未被记住的夏天
text.en: 1776 · A summer before the world knew his name

text.zh: 沿石路寻找伯尔；酒馆门前可以进入下一处场景。
text.en: Find Burr along the cobblestones; the tavern entrance leads to the next scene.

context: field: title / field: points / field: street

text.zh: 街口 · 相识
text.en: Crossroads · An introduction

context: field: body / field: points / field: street

text.zh: 伯尔站在街口，打量着往来的人。
text.en: Burr stands at the crossroads, watching the passersby.

context: field: title / field: points / field: street

text.zh: 酒馆 · 城市的声音
text.en: Tavern · Voices of the city

context: field: body / field: points / field: street

text.zh: 门内的杯盏声里，夹着关于独立的争论。
text.en: Between the clinking cups, voices argue about independence.

context: field: title / field: points / field: street

text.zh: 水岸 · 新世界的入口
text.en: Waterfront · A door to the new world

context: field: body / field: points / field: street

text.zh: 船带来货物，也带来旧世界的消息。
text.en: Ships bring cargo, and news from the old world.

context: field: title / field: exits / field: street

text.zh: 进入酒馆
text.en: Enter the tavern

text.zh: 酒馆，未熄的火
text.en: The tavern, a fire still burning

text.zh: 第二幕 · 革命的同伴
text.en: ACT II · COMPANY OF REVOLUTION

text.zh: 1776 · 举杯之前，先交换一个念头
text.en: 1776 · Before a toast, an exchange of ideas

text.zh: 绕过长桌，看看炉火、手稿与杯盏。靠近标记按 E 查看。
text.en: Walk among the tables, hearth and manuscripts. Press E near a marker to inspect.

context: field: title / field: points / field: tavern

text.zh: 长桌 · 同伴的席位
text.en: The long table · Seats for companions

context: field: body / field: points / field: tavern

text.zh: 四只杯子围着摊开的报纸。劳伦斯、拉法耶特与穆里根的座位还空着；这一桌将把各自的雄心，变成共同的行动。
text.en: Four cups surround an open newspaper. The seats of Laurens, Lafayette and Mulligan are still empty; around this table, separate ambitions will become a common cause.

context: field: title / field: points / field: tavern

text.zh: 炉火 · 城里的传闻
text.en: The hearth · Rumors in the city

context: field: body / field: points / field: tavern

text.zh: 柴火在砖炉里燃烧。港口封锁、军需短缺、独立的消息，都曾在这里被低声重复，再被带到街上。
text.en: Logs burn in the brick hearth. Word of blockades, shortages and independence has passed quietly through this room before reaching the streets.

context: field: title / field: points / field: tavern

text.zh: 手稿 · 尚未发出的声音
text.en: The manuscript · A voice not yet heard

context: field: body / field: points / field: tavern

text.zh: 蜡烛照着未写完的段落。把激动写成一句能说服人的话，比高声喊出它更难。一页草稿，也许就是明天街头争论的开始。
text.en: A candle lights an unfinished paragraph. Turning conviction into a persuasive sentence is harder than shouting it. A draft on this desk may begin tomorrow’s argument in the streets.

context: field: title / field: exits / field: tavern

text.zh: 回到纽约街角
text.en: Return to the New York street

context: field: title / field: exits / field: tavern

text.zh: 前往辩论广场
text.en: Continue to the debate square

text.zh: 广场，众声之中
text.en: The square, among many voices

text.zh: 第三幕 · 公开辩论
text.en: ACT III · PUBLIC DEBATE

text.zh: 1776 · 让一句话穿过整座广场
text.en: 1776 · Let a sentence carry across the square

text.zh: 从印刷摊绕到讲台前，广场另一侧的路通往军营。
text.en: Explore the print stall and the speaking platform. A road on the far side leads to camp.

context: field: title / field: points / field: square

text.zh: 讲台 · 公开的立场
text.en: The platform · A public position

context: field: body / field: points / field: square

text.zh: 木台略高于人群的视线。支持者和反对者将从两侧聚拢：论点必须清楚，停顿也必须有分量。
text.en: The timber platform stands just above the crowd’s eye line. Supporters and opponents will gather on either side: arguments must be clear, and pauses must carry weight.

context: field: title / field: points / field: square

text.zh: 印刷摊 · 纸上的战场
text.en: The print stall · A battlefield on paper

context: field: body / field: points / field: square

text.zh: 铅字、纸张与墨，把一个人的意见变成许多人手中的传单。街头的辩论在这里获得第二种声音。
text.en: Type, paper and ink turn one person’s opinion into leaflets carried by many. Here, a street debate acquires a second voice.

context: field: title / field: points / field: square

text.zh: 告示板 · 人群将去向何处
text.en: The noticeboard · Where people will go

context: field: body / field: points / field: square

text.zh: 招募与集会的告示一层盖着一层。从这里向外走，城市的争论逐渐变成军营里的命令。
text.en: Recruitment and meeting notices overlap on the board. Beyond this square, the city’s arguments begin to become orders in a military camp.

context: field: title / field: exits / field: square

text.zh: 返回酒馆
text.en: Return to the tavern

context: field: title / field: exits / field: square

text.zh: 前往华盛顿军营
text.en: Continue to Washington’s camp

text.zh: 军营，暮色下的命令
text.en: The camp, orders at dusk

text.zh: 第四幕 · 华盛顿的副官
text.en: ACT IV · WASHINGTON’S AIDE

text.zh: 1777 · 墨水与火药之间
text.en: 1777 · Between ink and gunpowder

text.zh: 沿营地通道查看指挥帐、补给和篝火，再前往约克镇。
text.en: Follow the camp paths to the command tent, supplies and fire, then continue to Yorktown.

context: field: title / field: points / field: camp

text.zh: 指挥帐 · 一纸军令
text.en: The command tent · Orders on paper

context: field: body / field: points / field: camp

text.zh: 地图被镇纸压住，路线停在烛光下。副官需要把将军的判断写成清晰的命令，让远处的部队也能准确执行。
text.en: Paperweights hold the map still, its routes caught in candlelight. An aide must turn the general’s judgment into clear orders that distant units can carry out precisely.

context: field: title / field: points / field: camp

text.zh: 辎重 · 战线的另一端
text.en: Supplies · The other end of the line

context: field: body / field: points / field: camp

text.zh: 车轮、粮桶与成排的木箱决定部队能走多远。每一次调动，都先是一道补给问题。
text.en: Wheels, provision barrels and rows of crates determine how far the army can move. Every maneuver begins as a question of supply.

context: field: title / field: points / field: camp

text.zh: 篝火 · 等待天亮
text.en: The campfire · Waiting for dawn

context: field: body / field: points / field: camp

text.zh: 帐篷之间留着一道暖光。信件从这里出发，也在这里被拆开；下一道命令到来之前，营地短暂地安静下来。
text.en: A warm glow remains between the tents. Letters leave from here and are opened here; before the next orders arrive, the camp briefly falls quiet.

context: field: title / field: exits / field: camp

text.zh: 返回辩论广场
text.en: Return to the debate square

context: field: title / field: exits / field: camp

text.zh: 前往约克镇
text.en: Continue to Yorktown

text.zh: 约克镇，夜色中的突破口
text.en: Yorktown, an opening in the night

text.zh: 第五幕 · 最后的冲锋
text.en: ACT V · THE FINAL ASSAULT

text.zh: 1781 · 越过工事，走向黎明
text.en: 1781 · Beyond the earthworks, toward dawn

text.zh: 沿战壕穿过炮位与工事缺口。中央通道可以进入堡垒内侧。
text.en: Follow the trench past the battery and through the earthworks. The central passage reaches the inner redoubt.

context: field: title / field: points / field: yorktown

text.zh: 集结处 · 屏息等待
text.en: The assembly point · Holding a breath

context: field: body / field: points / field: yorktown

text.zh: 队伍将在这里压低声音，等待出击的信号。前方的两道通路把掩体、炮位与堡垒连接起来。
text.en: The troops will gather here in hushed voices, waiting for the signal. Two routes ahead connect cover, batteries and the redoubt.

context: field: title / field: points / field: yorktown

text.zh: 炮位 · 火光后的间隙
text.en: The battery · A pause after the flash

context: field: body / field: points / field: yorktown

text.zh: 炮轮陷在泥里，弹药堆在手边。炮声之间的短暂间隙，决定何时能够离开掩体。
text.en: Gun wheels sink into the mud, ammunition stacked within reach. The brief intervals between shots determine when it is possible to leave cover.

context: field: title / field: points / field: yorktown

text.zh: 堡垒内侧 · 突破之后
text.en: Inside the redoubt · After the breach

context: field: body / field: points / field: yorktown

text.zh: 木桩与土墙不再挡住前路。从集结处到这里，路线已贯通；胜负将取决于每一步能否与同伴的行动一致。
text.en: Timber stakes and earth walls no longer block the way. The route from the assembly point is open; success will depend on each step matching the actions of others.
